newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa could face crisis of capacity - Mbeki.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa could face crisis of capacity - Mbeki.

text.p: South Africa's rollover of unspent funds from one fiscal year to the next was a symptom of a continuing inability to deliver services and infrastructure, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Thursday.

Mbeki told the National Council of Provinces, which replaced the senate in February, that the government had to cancel 50 civil engineering projects at provincial or lower levels in 1996 because there was no capacity to do the work.
He said the nine provinces would be responsible in the year to March 31, 1998, for spending 57 percent of South Africa's non-debt expenditure.
"The impact which provinces now have on the implementation of national policy is substantial.

"Well-aligned and complimentary policies and programmes of action, efficiently managed, will advance transformation. Lack of coordination and failure of capacity will seriously undermine progress," he said.

Commenting on Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget on Wednesday, Mbeki said the anticipated rollover of nine billion rand in unspent allocations from 1996/97 to the new financial year should be seen as a warning.
"Rollovers and unspent allocations are, in fact, symptoms of insufficient capacity to use allocated resources and we cannot say that there has been a significant improvement over the past year.
"Problems of this kind retard delivery, cause unnecessary expense through the borrowing of unused funds and dampen economic growth. We cannot allow this to continue," he said.
